categories.main_business_segments: Shanghai Model Organisms Center, Inc. (SMOC) primarily engages in the research, development, production, and sales of genetically modified animal models and related technical services. Its main business includes customized models, standardized models, model breeding, pharmacological evaluation and phenotypic analysis, feeding services, and other model organism technology services. The company serves both scientific research clients and industrial clients, with a focus on gene function research, drug discovery, and preclinical drug evaluation.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages four core technologies: CRISPR/Cas gene editing system, ES cell targeting technology, gene expression regulation technology, and assisted reproductive technology. It has developed proprietary gene editing enhancement systems and rapid ES cell line construction techniques. Production methods include transgenic model construction, gene knockout, knockin, point mutation, and conditional knockout models, combined with natural and assisted reproduction for model breeding. The company also operates advanced SPF animal facilities and employs comprehensive phenotypic and pharmacological evaluation platforms.
categories.primary_customers_markets: SMOC serves over 950 scientific research institutions and more than 720 industrial clients, including universities, research institutes, hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, and CROs. Its products and services support gene function research, disease mechanism studies, drug target validation, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and safety evaluation in preclinical drug development. The company targets markets in life sciences, biomedical research, and pharmaceutical R&D, including emerging fields like antibody drug development, cell therapy, and rare disease research.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in China with multiple production and R&D bases in Shanghai, Guangdong, and Beijing. It also has a wholly-owned subsidiary in the United States (Texas), serving as a base for operations and a biopharmaceutical incubator. SMOC actively expands its overseas market presence, including North America, Europe, Japan, France, and South Korea, with a growing overseas sales team and partnerships with international distributors.
categories.supply_chain_position: SMOC operates mainly in the midstream and downstream segments of the supply chain, focusing on the development, production, and supply of genetically modified animal models and related technical services. It provides customized and standardized animal models, breeding services, and preclinical pharmacological evaluation, supporting upstream pharmaceutical R&D and downstream clinical research activities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company emphasizes innovation-driven growth, focusing on optimizing gene editing technologies to improve editing efficiency and reduce off-target effects. It aims to expand its proprietary model library, especially humanized models for targeted therapies, rare diseases, and immunotherapies. SMOC is developing a full-process humanized antibody discovery platform and enhancing its pharmacological evaluation and antibody screening services. It plans to expand production capacity, improve information systems, deepen global market penetration, and strengthen talent development to sustain competitive advantage.
categories.revenue_model: SMOC generates revenue primarily through the sale of genetically modified animal models (customized and standardized), breeding services, and technical services such as pharmacological evaluation, phenotypic analysis, and feeding services. Revenue recognition occurs upon delivery and customer acceptance or after an objection period. The company also earns income from government subsidies, investment returns, and financial products. Overseas sales include direct sales and distributor-based models with revenue sharing.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company is a leading player in China's gene-modified animal model industry, competing with domestic firms like Yakang Bio, BioSciTech, and international companies such as Jackson Laboratory, Charles River, and Taconic. SMOC holds a strong market position with a large proprietary model library and advanced technology platforms. It is recognized for its innovation, scale, and comprehensive service offerings, maintaining a competitive edge in both domestic and international markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, SMOC reported operating revenue of approximately RMB 381.24 million, a 4.01% increase year-over-year, and achieved net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 6.5 million, turning profitable after previous losses. The company invested about 19.67% of revenue in R&D. It operates with total assets around RMB 1.93 billion and net assets of RMB 1.68 billion. Overseas revenue accounted for about 14% of total revenue, growing 32% year-over-year. The company has shown steady growth with improved profitability and cash flow.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: SMOC differentiates itself through a vast and diverse proprietary library of over 13,000 standardized models, including more than 940 humanized gene-modified mouse strains, supporting cutting-edge drug discovery and precision medicine. Its core technologies enable rapid, efficient, and high-quality model construction and breeding. The company offers integrated one-stop services from model construction to pharmacological evaluation and antibody discovery, backed by advanced SPF facilities and strong scientific expertise. Its focus on innovation, customization, and comprehensive service enhances customer satisfaction and loyalty.
